CubeRenderer.name: CubeRenderer
CubeRenderer.description:
A 1 x 1 x 1 cube (the built-in "Cube" mesh), unlit in its colour unless it has a material.
Opaque: a translucent colour doesn't blend; give it a material with alphaMode "blend" for that.

SphereRenderer.name: SphereRenderer
SphereRenderer.description:
A sphere of diameter 1 (the built-in "Sphere" mesh at the default subdivision), unlit in its colour unless it
has a material

QuadRenderer.name: QuadRenderer
QuadRenderer.description:
A 1 x 1 quad on the object's x/y plane, facing +Z (the built-in "Quad" mesh), unlit in its colour unless it
has a material

MeshRenderer.name: MeshRenderer
MeshRenderer.description:
Draws a mesh with one material per submesh. An empty slot draws lit white. Blend materials draw in the
Transparent queue, the rest in the Opaque queue.

Light.name: Light
Light.description:
A light the lit shaders use. Every active Light in the scene is collected each frame; a scene with none is lit by
a default directional light from the upper left and slightly behind (direction (0.5, -1, 0.3)).

ParticleSystem.name: ParticleSystem
ParticleSystem.description:
Emits and draws particles: small camera-facing quads that start at the object, fly under gravity and fade away
(see docs/particles.html). Particles exist only while the scene plays, are never saved, and freeze while the time
scale is 0. Settings apply at once, except Backend, MaxParticles and Seed, which are read when the system starts.

SoftBody.name: SoftBody
SoftBody.description:
Makes the MeshRenderer on the same object a soft body that squashes and wobbles under gravity (see
docs/soft-bodies.html). Needs a MeshRenderer with a mesh and no Rigidbody on the object. The body exists only while
the scene plays, is never saved, and freezes while the time scale is 0. Settings apply at once, except Backend and
Resolution, which are read when the body starts; Reset restarts it.

TextRenderer.name: TextRenderer
TextRenderer.description:
World-space text on the object's x/y plane, facing +Z, drawn with an SDF font in the Transparent queue.
Sizes are in world units. Changing a setting other than the colour lays the text out again on the next draw.

LuaComponent.name: LuaComponent
LuaComponent.description:
Runs a behaviour script: a file returning a table whose __index is itself, with optional
OnAttach, OnUpdate, OnFixedUpdate, OnLateUpdate, OnDestroy, OnEnable, OnDisable, collision methods and
the pointer methods OnMouseEnter, OnMouseOver, OnMouseExit, OnMouseDown, OnMouseDrag, OnMouseUp and
OnMouseUpAsButton (no arguments; sent before OnUpdate to the object under the cursor, left button only).
Inside those methods, self.gameObject and self.component are set.

Rect.name: Rect
Rect.description: A rectangle in canvas space: (x, y) is its bottom-left corner

RectTransform.name: RectTransform
RectTransform.description: Where a UI element sits in its parent's rect (Unity's RectTransform). One per object.

Canvas.name: Canvas
Canvas.description:
The root of a UI tree. A screen-space overlay canvas (the default) is drawn over the scene, and higher sort
orders draw on top and are hit first. A world-space canvas is a rectangle in the world, drawn with the scene's
transparent objects and hit by the camera's ray.

Image.name: Image
Image.description:
A coloured rectangle over its object's rect, optionally showing a sprite (an image file). A raycast target
(the default) takes the pointer: its object gets the OnMouse* callbacks and Input.IsPointerOverUI() is true.

UIText.name: UIText
UIText.description:
Text drawn inside its object's rect, with an SDF font. Sizes are canvas pixels. Unlike Image it is not a
raycast target by default, so a label lets the pointer through to what is underneath.
Changing a setting other than the colour, or the rect's width with wrap on, lays the text out again.

Button.name: Button
Button.description:
A clickable UI element: put it on an object with a raycast-target graphic (an Image). It tints its target
graphic for its state (the graphic's own colour times the state's colour times the multiplier, so the
graphic's colour itself never changes) and calls its OnClick listeners when the left button is pressed
and released over it, if it is interactable and enabled. Listeners are not saved with the scene.

Layers.name: Layers
Layers.description:
The project's 32 layers (as in Unity) and which of them collide. A layer mask has bit (1 << layer)
set for each layer it includes.

IgnoreRaycast.name: IgnoreRaycast
IgnoreRaycast.description: 2 ("Ignore Raycast"): left out of queries by default

Collision.name: Collision
Collision.description:
The argument of OnCollisionEnter/Stay/Exit. Safe to keep after the callback: its objects are
references like any other (see CORE OBJECTS).

rigidbody.name: rigidbody
rigidbody.description: The receiver's Rigidbody (nil for a static collider)

otherRigidbody.name: otherRigidbody
otherRigidbody.description: The other object's Rigidbody (nil for a static collider)

Trigger.name: Trigger
Trigger.description: The argument of OnTriggerEnter/Stay/Exit; safe to keep, like Collision

RaycastHit.name: RaycastHit
RaycastHit.description: A raycast hit. Safe to keep: its objects are references like any other (see CORE OBJECTS).

gameObject.name: gameObject
gameObject.description: The hit body's object (its Rigidbody's object for a compound body)

collider.name: collider
collider.description: The collider that was hit, as its own type (BoxCollider, ...)

disabled.name: disabled
disabled.description: Whether this action map is disabled

name.name: name
name.description: The name of this action map

Mouse.name: Mouse
Mouse.description:
The cursor and mouse buttons, sampled once at the start of each frame. Buttons are 0..7: 0 left, 1 right,
2 middle (out-of-range buttons read false).

tick.name: tick
tick.description: Fixed ticks begun so far (read-only): 0 before the first, N inside tick N's OnFixedUpdate

timeScale.name: timeScale
timeScale.description: Time scale multiplier (1.0 = normal, 0.5 = slow motion, 0.0 = paused)

Random.Float.description: Generate a random float between 0 and 1

Random.Range.name: Random.Range

GameObject.SetLayer.description:

children keep their own layer. Values outside 0..31 are clamped, with a warning.

GameObject.SetLayerRecursive.name: GameObject.SetLayerRecursive
GameObject.SetLayerRecursive.description: Set the layer of this GameObject and all its descendants

GameObject.AddComponent.name: GameObject.AddComponent
GameObject.AddComponent.description:
Add a component by type name and return it.

"SphereRenderer", "QuadRenderer", "MeshRenderer", "TextRenderer", "ParticleSystem", "SoftBody", "Light", "AudioSource", "AudioListener",
"LuaComponent", "RectTransform", "Canvas", "Image", "UIText", "Button". Unknown names raise an error.

GameObject.GetComponent.description: Get a component by type name (same names as AddComponent)

returns.description: nil when the object has no component of that type

CubeRenderer.SetMaterial.name: CubeRenderer.SetMaterial
CubeRenderer.SetMaterial.description:
A .mat file the cube draws with, tinted by its colour; nil goes back to unlit in the colour.
Raises an error (keeping the current material) if it doesn't load.

SphereRenderer.SetSubdivision.name: SphereRenderer.SetSubdivision
SphereRenderer.SetSubdivision.description: Mesh quality (16 x 32 by default); takes effect on the next draw

params.name: path
params.description: a .mat file, or nil for unlit in the colour

params.name: path
params.description: a .mat file, or nil for unlit in the colour

MeshRenderer.SetMesh.name: MeshRenderer.SetMesh
MeshRenderer.SetMesh.description:
A built-in mesh by name, or a mesh asset's path (a model's mesh is "<model path>#<key>"); nil clears it. Raises an
error (keeping the current mesh) if it doesn't load.

MeshRenderer.GetMesh.name: MeshRenderer.GetMesh
MeshRenderer.GetMesh.description: model's mesh, "" for a mesh made at runtime); nil without a mesh

returns.description: nameOrPath the built-in's name or the asset's path ("res://models/robot.glb#mesh/Body" for a

MeshRenderer.GetMaterialCount.name: MeshRenderer.GetMaterialCount
MeshRenderer.GetMaterialCount.description: The number of material slots that draw: the mesh's submesh count (0 without a mesh)

MeshRenderer.SetMaterial.name: MeshRenderer.SetMaterial
MeshRenderer.SetMaterial.description:
Sets material slot `index` (1-based) to a .mat file or a model's material ("res://models/robot.glb#material/Paint"),
or empties it with nil. Raises an error (keeping the slot) if it doesn't load.

returns.description: path nil for an empty slot

MeshRenderer.GetBounds.name: MeshRenderer.GetBounds
MeshRenderer.GetBounds.description: The mesh's bounds in its own space (before the object's transform)

params.name: type
params.description: an unknown name raises an error and changes nothing

Light.SetDirection.name: Light.SetDirection
Light.SetDirection.description:
A directional light's direction of travel in world space, e.g. Vector3(0.4, -0.6, -0.7) shines down and away
from a camera on +Z (need not be normalized; default (0, -1, 0))

params.name: color
params.description: r, g and b are used; alpha is ignored

params.name: range
params.description: point and spot lights: how far the light reaches, in world units (default 10)

ParticleSystem.Play.name: ParticleSystem.Play
ParticleSystem.Play.description: Starts emitting: the emission rate, and the burst once

ParticleSystem.Stop.name: ParticleSystem.Stop
ParticleSystem.Stop.description: Stops emitting; the particles already flying finish their lives

ParticleSystem.EmitBurst.name: ParticleSystem.EmitBurst
ParticleSystem.EmitBurst.description: Starts `count` particles now, playing or not. Particles beyond maxParticles are dropped (one warning in the log).

ParticleSystem.GetActiveBackend.name: ParticleSystem.GetActiveBackend
ParticleSystem.GetActiveBackend.description: The backend that simulates this system: "CPU", or "PhysX" when the GPU particle backend is in use

returns.description: nil until the system has started (the scene is playing)

params.name: backend
params.description: Auto: PhysX when the GPU physics scene is up, else CPU. PhysX falls back to CPU, with one warning, where there is no GPU backend. An unknown name raises an error.

returns.description: what was asked for (GetActiveBackend says what is used)

params.name: material
params.description: what the particles are made of on the PhysX backend (a PBD material preset: Water flows and pools, Sand piles up, Smoke drifts); the CPU backend ignores it. Read when the system starts. An unknown name raises an error.

params.name: playOnAwake
params.description: emit as soon as the system starts (default true)

params.name: maxParticles
params.description: the most particles alive at once (default 1000, at most 100000); more are dropped

params.name: seed
params.description: the same seed gives the same particles (default 1)

params.name: count
params.description: particles started at once by every Play (default 0)

params.name: shape
params.description: a cone along the object's +Y axis, or a sphere (default Cone). An unknown name raises an error.

params.name: radius
params.description: the cone's base disc, or the sphere, in world units (default 0)

params.name: angle
params.description: the cone's half angle in degrees (default 25)

ParticleSystem.SetLifetime.name: ParticleSystem.SetLifetime
ParticleSystem.SetLifetime.description: Each particle's lifetime is picked from this range when it starts

ParticleSystem.SetSpeed.name: ParticleSystem.SetSpeed
ParticleSystem.SetSpeed.description: Each particle's start speed is picked from this range

ParticleSystem.SetSize.name: ParticleSystem.SetSize
ParticleSystem.SetSize.description: A particle's quad edge goes from `start` to `end` over its life

params.name: color
params.description: the colour at death; alpha 0 fades the particle out (default white, alpha 0)

params.name: drag
params.description: the share of the velocity lost per second (default 0)

ParticleSystem.SetGround.name: ParticleSystem.SetGround
ParticleSystem.SetGround.description: Particles bounce off the plane y = height (world space), the only collision the CPU backend does

params.name: bounce
params.description: the share of its speed a particle keeps, 0 to 1 (default 0.3)

params.name: mode
params.description: Additive adds the particles to the picture (drawn as Alpha by the software renderer, which can't blend)

params.name: path
params.description: an image file, e.g. "res://particles/spark.png"; nil draws plain colours. A path that doesn't load raises an error and keeps the current texture.

returns.description: the texture's path, nil without one

SoftBody.AddVelocity.name: SoftBody.AddVelocity
SoftBody.AddVelocity.description: Adds a velocity to the whole body; does nothing before it started

SoftBody.Reset.name: SoftBody.Reset
SoftBody.Reset.description: Puts the body back to its rest shape at the object's current pose, at rest (it restarts, so the backend is chosen again)

returns.description: name "CPU" or "PhysX": the backend simulating the body; "" when it is inert (no MeshRenderer, a Rigidbody, a mesh that can't be tetrahedralised) or hasn't started

params.name: backend
params.description: Auto: the PhysX GPU backend when there is one, else CPU. Read when the body starts. An unknown name raises an error.

params.name: resolution
params.description: voxels along the longest axis of the mesh, 2 to 32 (default 10). Read when the body starts.

params.name: density
params.description: mass per unit volume in kg/m^3 (default 1000)

params.name: stiffness
params.description: Young's modulus in pascals (default 100000; rubber is about 1e6)

params.name: poisson
params.description: Poisson's ratio, 0 to 0.49: how much the body keeps its volume (default 0.3)

params.name: iterations
params.description: solver iterations in each of the CPU backend's 4 sub-steps (default 2)

SoftBody.SetGround.name: SoftBody.SetGround
SoftBody.SetGround.description: The body rests on the plane y = height (world space), the only collision the CPU backend does

SoftBody.SetMaterialModel.name: SoftBody.SetMaterialModel
SoftBody.SetMaterialModel.description: Used only by the PhysX backend (a later stage); the CPU backend ignores it

SoftBody.SetSelfCollision.name: SoftBody.SetSelfCollision
SoftBody.SetSelfCollision.description: Used only by the PhysX backend (a later stage); the CPU backend ignores it

Model.Instantiate.name: Model.Instantiate
Model.Instantiate.description:
A new instance of a model's hierarchy: a root object (named after the file) with one child object per node,
each with its node's name and local transform, and a MeshRenderer for each node with a mesh. Under `parent` when
given (at its origin); otherwise in no scene yet, owned by the script until a scene or parent holds it.
Raises an error if the model doesn't load.

params.name: width
params.description: wrap width in world units; 0 (the default) never wraps

params.name: spacing
params.description: extra space between glyphs, in ems (default 0; negative tightens)

TextRenderer.SetOutline.name: TextRenderer.SetOutline
TextRenderer.SetOutline.description:
An outline around the glyphs, drawn under them. Lengths are in ems; effects are limited to 90% of the
font's SDF spread (1/6 em for the default font: about 0.15 em), with one warning when reduced.

params.name: width
params.description: outline width in ems; 0 (the default) turns it off

TextRenderer.SetShadow.name: TextRenderer.SetShadow
TextRenderer.SetShadow.description: A shadow under the text (with offset 0 and some softness, a glow). Off while the colour's alpha is 0 (the default).

params.name: softness
params.description: how far its edge fades, in ems (default 0; ignored by the software renderer)

params.name: softness
params.description: how far the outer edges fade, in ems (default 0 = crisp; ignored by the software renderer)

TextRenderer.AddEffectPass.name: TextRenderer.AddEffectPass
TextRenderer.AddEffectPass.signature: TextRenderer:AddEffectPass(offsetX, offsetY, color, width, softness, order)
TextRenderer.AddEffectPass.description:
An extra effect pass: the glyph shape drawn in one colour behind the face, placed by its order (by default in
front of the shadow, the outline and the passes added before it). The shape is the glyph grown outward by `width`, moved by the offset. With only
an offset it is a shadow, with a width an outline, with softness and no offset a glow. Saved with the scene;
each pass is one more draw, so keep the list short. Limited to the font's SDF spread like the other effects.
shadow is at -200 and the settings outline at -100, so an order below -200 draws behind the shadow. The face is
drawn after every pass, so an order above 0 is not supported: it counts as 0, with one warning.

params.name: color
params.description: a colour with alpha 0 draws nothing

params.name: width
params.description: ems outward from the glyph edge (default 0)

params.name: softness
params.description: how far its edge fades, in ems (default 0; ignored by the software renderer)

params.name: order
params.description: where it sits in the back-to-front list (default 0; lower draws further back). The settings

TextRenderer.ClearEffectPasses.name: TextRenderer.ClearEffectPasses
TextRenderer.ClearEffectPasses.description: Removes every extra pass; the shadow, outline and softness settings stay.

TextRenderer.SetAlignment.name: TextRenderer.SetAlignment
TextRenderer.SetAlignment.description: Where the block sits relative to the object's origin. Unknown names raise an error and change nothing.

TextRenderer.SetFont.name: TextRenderer.SetFont
TextRenderer.SetFont.description:
Draw with a font file; nil goes back to the built-in default font. Raises an error, keeping the
current font, if the file doesn't load.

TextRenderer.GetBounds.name: TextRenderer.GetBounds
TextRenderer.GetBounds.description: The laid-out block in the object's local units (all 0 for empty text)

LuaComponent.HasMissingScript.name: LuaComponent.HasMissingScript
LuaComponent.HasMissingScript.description: True when the script is missing, failed to load, or didn't return a table

Component.IsValid.name: Component.IsValid
Component.IsValid.description:
False once this component is destroyed (removed, its GameObject destroyed, or the scene unloaded);
the other methods then raise an error

Component.IsDestroyed.name: Component.IsDestroyed
Component.IsDestroyed.description: True once this component is destroyed (the opposite of IsValid)

Component.GetGameObject.description: The GameObject this component is attached to

Component.SetActive.description: Set whether this component is active

RectTransform.GetRect.description: The rect the last layout resolved (each UI pass and each pointer update); zeros before any

Canvas.SetRenderMode.name: Canvas.SetRenderMode
Canvas.SetRenderMode.description:
"WorldSpace" adds a transform (at the origin, scale 1) and a RectTransform if the object has none. An unknown
name raises an error and changes nothing.

Canvas.GetSize.name: Canvas.GetSize
Canvas.GetSize.description:
A world canvas's size in canvas units: its RectTransform's sizeDelta (100 x 100 without one). Its transform's
scale is the size of a canvas unit in world units (0.01 from UI.CreateCanvas).

Canvas.SetSize.name: Canvas.SetSize
Canvas.SetSize.description: Sets the RectTransform's sizeDelta, adding a RectTransform if the object has none

params.name: raycastTarget
params.description: false lets the pointer through to what is underneath

Image.SetSprite.name: Image.SetSprite
Image.SetSprite.description:
Show an image file (PNG, JPEG, TGA or BMP) in the rect, multiplied by the colour; nil clears it. Raises an
error, keeping the current sprite, if the file doesn't load. Saved with the scene.

Image.GetSprite.name: Image.GetSprite
Image.GetSprite.description: The sprite's path ("res://..." for a project asset), or nil without a sprite

params.name: raycastTarget
params.description: true makes the text take the pointer (default false)

params.name: wrap
params.description: whether lines wrap at the rect's width (default true)

params.name: spacing
params.description: extra space between glyphs, in ems (default 0; negative tightens)

UIText.SetOutline.name: UIText.SetOutline
UIText.SetOutline.description:
An outline around the glyphs, drawn under them. Lengths are in ems (fontSize pixels each); effects are
limited to 90% of the font's SDF spread (about 0.15 em for the default font), with one warning when reduced.

params.name: width
params.description: outline width in ems; 0 (the default) turns it off

UIText.SetShadow.name: UIText.SetShadow
UIText.SetShadow.description: A shadow under the text (with offset 0 and some softness, a glow). Off while the colour's alpha is 0 (the default).

params.name: softness
params.description: how far its edge fades, in ems (default 0; ignored by the software renderer)

params.name: softness
params.description: how far the outer edges fade, in ems (default 0 = crisp; ignored by the software renderer)

UIText.AddEffectPass.description:
An extra effect pass: the glyph shape drawn in one colour behind the face, placed by its order (by default in
front of the shadow, the outline and the passes added before it). The shape is the glyph grown outward by `width`, moved by the offset. With only
an offset it is a shadow, with a width an outline, with softness and no offset a glow. Saved with the scene;
each pass is one more draw, so keep the list short. Limited to the font's SDF spread like the other effects.
shadow is at -200 and the settings outline at -100, so an order below -200 draws behind the shadow. The face is
drawn after every pass, so an order above 0 is not supported: it counts as 0, with one warning.

params.name: color
params.description: a colour with alpha 0 draws nothing

params.name: width
params.description: ems outward from the glyph edge (default 0)

params.name: softness
params.description: how far its edge fades, in ems (default 0; ignored by the software renderer)

params.name: order
params.description: where it sits in the back-to-front list (default 0; lower draws further back). The settings

Camera.ScreenPointToRay.name: Camera.ScreenPointToRay

The ray through a screen point, from the near plane away from the camera (unit direction). Takes window
coordinates (top-left origin, y down), as Input.GetMousePosition returns. The viewport defaults to the
window's size; pass both width and height to use another (only one of them is an error).
local mouse = Input.GetMousePosition()
local ray = Camera.Main():ScreenPointToRay(mouse.x, mouse.y)
local hit = Physics.Raycast(ray.origin, ray.direction, 100)
